Title: Kennedy tells anti-vaccine activists they have a friend in Trump's White House
Article_Text:
Kennedy tells anti-vaccine activists they have a friend in Trump's White House
WASHINGTON — Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. gave the keynote address Thursday at a conference of an anti-vaccine activist group he once chaired, telling the hundreds in attendance that they had a friend in President Donald Trump's White House.
It was Kennedy's first time appearing at the Children's Health Defense conference since he became secretary. Kennedy took leave from the group when he launched his bid to become president in 2023, but his speech Thursday served as a sort of homecoming, offering him a platform from which to hail the administration's steps to scale back vaccine guidance and reassure the activists in attendance that he was working to turn their priorities into policy.
“Let me be clear: You have a strong and steadfast friend in the White House. We've accomplished in 19 months things that would have seemed unthinkable two years ago,” he said.
The speech, peppered with questions about long established vaccine safety, also highlighted how once fringe views on vaccines have been given a prominent pulpit under the Trump administration.
Kennedy boasted about the administration's moves to downsize the childhood vaccination schedule and reshape a key vaccine advisory board — steps that have since been halted by a judge.
Kennedy lauded Trump for pushing ahead with attempts to overhaul vaccine guidance, including an executive order last month calling for spacing out the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, against medical groups' recommendations.
That executive order and now Kennedy's keynote speech at the Children's Health Defense conference mark a pivot by the White House and the Department of Health and Human Services, who earlier this year had appeared to be moving beyond vaccine efforts and toward a less contentious agenda on healthy food ahead of November’s midterm elections. HHS promoted the speech on its social media channels.
Kennedy, a longtime anti-vaccine activist, chaired Children’s Health Defense for years. He served as the group’s chief legal counsel and expanded it. After becoming health secretary last year, Kennedy moved at a blistering pace to overhaul public health guidance and revamp long-held precedents in vaccine policymaking.
Critics, among them many of the country's top medical associations, have said the moves risk stoking vaccine hesitancy and sowing confusion among Americans who endured a crisis of trust in their public health agencies following the COVID-19 pandemic. That public confidence continues to erode.
“We have not taken vaccines away from anybody. We have preserved access. But we have started asking the questions that you and millions of American parents have been asking for years,” Kennedy told the group.
Mary Holland, the CEO of Children’s Health Defense, referred to Kennedy as “Bobby” and said the group has “gratitude beyond words” to the HHS secretary for “recognizing there are real consequential issues around childhood vaccinations.”
Kennedy's appearance Thursday comes as the country faces its worst year for measles since 1991 and has seen seven reported measles-associated deaths in the last two years — more than the combined total of reported deaths over the previous three decades.
Pennsylvania officials have reported four measles-associated deaths this year. None of the four were vaccinated, according to the state health department. When state officials last month announced the first two of those deaths, it ignited a public feud between Gov. Josh Shapiro and Kennedy.
Shapiro blasted Kennedy's appearance on the social media site X Thursday, saying Kennedy “chose to spend his time today addressing the premier vaccine-denial conference in America.”
Shapiro said the HHS secretary should have encouraged people to get vaccinated for measles, "yet he couldn’t bring himself to do it. Instead, he pushed a narrative that continues to stoke fear and mistrust.”
A representative from the White House did not respond to an Associated Press request for comment on Kennedy’s appearance at the event.
Following Kennedy onstage Thursday was Andrew Wakefield, an author of a since-discredited study that linked the MMR vaccine to autism, which has fueled the anti-vaccine movement even though it was retracted.
Widespread scientific consensus and decades of studies have firmly concluded there is no link between vaccines and autism.
Shaughnessy Naughton, founder of 314 Action, a group that recruits scientists to run for public office, said Kennedy's decision to give a speech at the conference shows “the lack of seriousness he brings to HHS.”
"With a deadly measles outbreak killing people in Pennsylvania, the best thing Kennedy can do for Americans is step aside.”

Title: The T. rex had a body temperature similar to our own, study finds
Article_Text:
Using fossilized teeth, scientists have finally taken the T. rex's temperature — and it wasn't too different from our own.
Researchers once thought that dinosaurs were sluggish, cold-blooded creatures. Later findings challenged that, suggesting that older dinosaurs were warm-blooded and could control their body temperature.
Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10.
Most scientists agree that Tyrannosaurus rex was warm-blooded, but pinning down the exact core temperature of an extinct creature is difficult.
“We can't just use a thermometer to do that,” said Jasmina Wiemann, a paleobiologist at Johns Hopkins University who had no role in the latest work.
Scientists tried other methods like studying how T. rex grew or searching for clues in its bones, but a firm number eluded them.
In a new study, researchers hunted for chemical clues in the fearsome predator's teeth. It turns out that atoms within the enamel clump together in different patterns based on an animal's body temperature.
“We figured out how warm the most famous animal of all, a T. rex, was,” said co-author Aradhna Tripati, a geochemist at the University of California, Los Angeles.
Readings from three teeth revealed an average body temperature of about 97 degrees Fahrenheit (36 degrees Celsius). That's similar to modern elephants and not too far from the average body temperature of humans, which ranges from 97 to 99 degrees Fahrenheit (36 to 37 degrees Celsius).
The findings were published Wednesday in the journal Science Advances.
“I almost would have expected a higher body temperature,” Wiemann said. Based on her prior work, she thought the predator could have run a few degrees hotter — similar to modern birds, dinosaurs' warm-blooded descendants.
Knowing how hot or cold the T. rex was can help scientists piece together how the dinosaur might have lived.
At 97 degrees (36 degrees Celsius), T. rex could have lived across most of prehistoric North America, Tripati said, maintaining a stable internal thermometer across both cooler and hotter regions. The findings could also shed light on the kinds of prey the dinosaur had to hunt in order to keep its energy up.
Scientists say it'll be important to test these methods on other dinosaurs to see how warm or cold they ran. It's possible T. rex's temperature could have been one of the keys to its dominance as one of the dinosaur age's top predators.
“There's lots of interesting, charismatic species that could be explored using this,” said study co-author Robert Eagle, a geobiologist at UCLA.

Title: After ending winless ruts, NYCFC, Red Bulls meet for high-stakes derby
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
18 Sep 2026, 02:35 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Mark Smith)
Bragging rights in the Hudson River Derby might be secondary given the precarious nature of the playoff positioning for New York City FC and the New York Red Bulls when the teams convene Friday night at Yankee Stadium.
Both teams have nine games remaining and are separated by two points after stopping lengthy winless skids last week.
NYCFC (8-9-8, 32 points) begin the week in eighth and own the goal differential tiebreaker over ninth-place Cincinnati since they have outscored opponents 39-33, while Cincinnati has been outscored 59-52. NYCFC trail seventh-place Philadelphia by one point and sixth-place Orlando by two points, and those teams also have nine games remaining.
New York City heads into Friday 1-3-4 over the past eight matches. The Pigeons earned their first win since July 25 on Saturday with a 2-0 victory at Real Salt Lake, when Nicolas Fernandez and Luighi scored on either side of the halftime break.
'I think we found quite a decent balance when we play against the Red Bulls, but we're also very aware of what's at stake,' NYCFC coach Pascal Jansen said. 'It's a derby, it's emotional, means a lot to our fans from both sides. So it's going to be an intense game no matter what and for us, it's mainly about making sure we keep things under control, stick to the plan that we will make and make sure we get a good result.'
The Red Bulls (8-11-6, 30 points) sit in 10th and are two points behind NYCFC and Cincinnati while carrying a minus-15 goal differential. New York is attempting to win consecutive matches for just the third time this season and the first time since May 9-13.
Like their rivals, the Red Bulls ended a lengthy winless rut (0-4-2) Saturday with a 1-0 victory at Columbus. Ronald Donkor broke the stalemate in the 89th minute with his second goal of the year.
'We have not had enough to show for ourselves on certain days,' Red Bulls coach Michael Bradley said. 'We feel really good that now in this week-long road trip we take four points, two shutouts, and so, we are going to use this as a way to really build momentum.'
--Field Level Media

Title: Knicks pause ticket sales after error led to high prices
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
18 Sep 2026, 01:35 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Brenden Willsch)
The New York Knicks halted ticket sales on Thursday after an internal error led to some sky-high prices.
The get-in price for tickets to the Knicks' season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers is $1,251, according to TicketData.com.
The team plans to roll out lower prices early next week.
'We are pausing Knicks individual ticket sales due to a mistake in our pricing,' Madison Square Garden Sports said in a statement. 'We are rolling back to last year's prices plus an average increase of 12%. We will restart sales with new prices shortly, and anyone who already purchased individual tickets will be refunded the difference.'
The Knicks, led by guard Jalen Brunson, are coming off their first NBA title in 53 years so a price increase was expected.
But when the Knicks opened up single-game tickets on Wednesday, the get-in price for the Oct. 20 opener against the 76ers at Madison Square Garden hit $1,363. The figure had spiked as high as $1,408 this week when single-game tickets were first made available to Knicks Fan First Chase cardholders on Monday.
'Our intention was never to overcharge our loyal fans, and we thank everyone for their support of the Knicks and their patience as we get this right,' MSG said.
The contest with the 76ers is highly anticipated after Philadelphia signed LeBron James and acquired Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics over the offseason to make for a powerhouse foursome with Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.
The average get-in price for the Knicks' 45 scheduled preseason and regular season home games is currently $262. That is more than double that of any other team, with tickets to get into Los Angeles Lakers home games averaging $130, followed by the Celtics at $99.
At the other end of the spectrum, the current average get-in price for Charlotte Hornets and Memphis Grizzlies home games both sit at just $23.
The Knicks won last year's title by beating the San Antonio Spurs in five games in the NBA Finals.
--Field Level Media

Title: USMNT camp highlighted by presence of 16-year-old F Cavan Sullivan
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
18 Sep 2026, 01:25 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Vincent Carchietta)
After taking MLS by storm over the past two months, 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan will get his first chance to play with the United States men's national team when it reconvenes this weekend at Atlanta.
The USMNT will take the field for the first time since the World Cup when it faces Peru on Sept. 26 at Orlando, Chile on Sept. 29 at St. Louis, Mexico on Oct. 3 at Glendale, Ariz., and Canada Oct. 6 in St. Paul, Minn.
Sullivan, who has put a charge into the Philadelphia Union of late, will headline a group of young players being introduced to national team duty. The other half of the team will be made up of USMNT veterans, although forwards Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun will not be on the squad.
Head coach Mauricio Pochettino stressed that the roster in no way represents the group that has priority heading toward the next World Cup in 2030.
'The 28 players that are going to be involved in these four games, for different circumstances, are the best players we want see and we want to work with. That's it,' Pochettino said at a press conference in New York on Thursday.
Pochettino will have 28 players in camp, with 13 of those seeking their first USMNT appearance.
Sullivan, a Philadelphia native, has shown his promise with six goals and 11 assists in 23 matches (16 starts) this season. He has goal contributions in seven consecutive games to lead Philadelphia's 10-game unbeaten run since the end of the World Cup break.
Among other players invited to USMNT camp for the first time are defender Neil Pierre, Sullivan's Union teammate, midfielder Zavier Gozo of English side Crystal Palace and forward Julian Hall of the New York Red Bulls, all of whom are 19 or younger.
Those players will get their first taste of USMNT culture alongside World Cup participants in Sebastian Berhalter, Alex Freeman, Gio Reyna, Auston Trusty and Malik Tillman.
'This is the beginning of a fresh start for everyone, and we are excited in these first matches to bring a group of experienced players along with some young talents who have great potential,' Pochettino said.
The United States got off to a promising start at the World Cup with a dominating victory over Paraguay before going through the red-card controversy created when Balogun was ejected from a knockout-round victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina only to be reinstated for the round-of-16 game against Belgium.
The USMNT was eliminated in a lackluster 4-1 loss to Belgium.
'It's a completely different approach than it was in the past,' Pochettino said of the start to another World Cup cycle. 'The World Cup is in four years. We need to work with different objectives and goals.'
--Field Level Media

Title: Xander Bogaerts falls short of cycle as red-hot Padres torch Rockies
Article_Text:
Xander Bogaerts falls short of cycle as red-hot Padres torch Rockies
Big News Network.com
Xander Bogaerts falls short of cycle as red-hot Padres torch Rockies
(Photo credit: Isaiah J. Downing)
Xander Bogaerts homered and tripled in a seven-run second inning and finished a single shy of the cycle, and the surging San Diego Padres beat the Colorado Rockies 9-2 in Denver on Thursday.
Ty France and Dustin Harris also had three hits apiece and Jake Cronenworth and Samad Taylor each had two hits for San Diego (84-69), which finished 11-2 against Colorado this season.
The Padres have won 10 of 11 to increase their lead to four games over idle Arizona for the third and final NL wild-card berth.
San Diego is a game behind the Chicago Cubs for the top seed and a half-game back of Philadelphia for the second berth. The Phillies played at the New York Mets on Thursday night.
Michael King (12-9) tossed six solid innings, ending his day when he struck out Troy Johnston with the bases loaded and two outs. He allowed two runs on seven hits and two walks and fanned six.
Mickey Moniak and Brett Sullivan had two hits each for the Rockies (56-97), who have dropped 10 of 11 and are on pace for a fourth consecutive 100-loss season.
Jake McCarthy led off the bottom of the first with a triple and scored on Connor Norby's single to make it 1-0, but it disappeared when the Padres jumped on Colorado starter Tanner Gordon.
Bogaerts started the rally with a leadoff homer, his 12th of the season, and San Diego loaded the bases with a single and two walks.
Harris drove in a pair with a single to center, Manny Machado hit a sacrifice fly and France singled to left to put runners on the corners with two outs. Rockies right fielder Zac Veen had two fielding mistakes that resulted in back-to-back triples for Jackson Merrill and Bogaerts to make it 7-0.
Gordon (1-5) allowed seven runs on 10 hits in three innings.
The Padres added two more in the fifth when Taylor followed Cronenworth's leadoff triple with a double, and he scored on a Harris single.
Colorado scored in the sixth on a two-out single by Kyle Karros.
--Field Level Media

Title: Dolphins vs. 49ers: Where can I watch the game? Week 2 TV coverage map
Article_Text:
The Miami Dolphins visit the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, hoping to bounce back from a flat performance against the Las Vegas Raiders last week. While Miami wants things to be different this week, there is at least one aspect of the game that will look very familiar. The television coverage map for Week 2 is just a slightly expanded version of Miami’s Week 1 regional broadcast area.
Where can I watch the Dolphins vs. 49ers game?
The Miami Dolphins at San Francisco 49ers game will be broadcast in a limited region.
Miami is once again in a late time slot, with FOX handling the broadcast. Kevin Kugler and Daryl Johnston will be on the call.
Where will the Dolphins vs. the 49ers game air on TV?
In Florida, the game will be relegated to the southern end of the state. Miami, West Palm Beach, and Fort Myers are the only markets scheduled to air the game
Moving out west, we see a bigger slice of the country getting a chance to see the Dolphins - though it is still a regional broadcast. The 49ers’ impact on the game leads to all of California, save San Diego, picking up the broadcast. From there, most of Nevada (outside of Las Vegas), all of Utah, and the border areas of Wyoming, Idaho, and Oregon will have the game.
What other games will I see in Florida?
1 p.m. Eastern time slot
During the early slot, fans in Florida may have options - though those options differ across the state. CBS will air the Pittsburgh Steelers at the New England Patriots game in Miami and West Palm Beach, In Fort Myers and Tampa, the Cleveland Browns at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be broadcast. Continuing north, most of the rest of the state will not have a CBS game in the early slot, saving space for a late-game CBS broadcast.
The western end of the panhandle will pick up the New Orleans Saints at the Baltimore Ravens game.
On FOX, Miami, West Palm Beach, and Fort Myers will see the Green Bay Packers at New York Jets game. Central Florida, including Tampa and Orlando, will have the Minnesota Vikings at the Chicago Bears. The Jacksonville and Tallahassee markets will see the Carolina Panthers at Atlanta Falcons broadcast. Pensacola and west along the panhandle will feature the Philadelphia Eagles at the Tennessee Titans game.
4:05/4:25 p.m. Eastern time slot
CBS only has a single-game broadcast in Week 2. The only game on CBS in the late slot in Florida is the Jacksonville Jaguars at the Denver Broncos game, filling the space that had no broadcast in the early slot. These markets include Orlando, Jacksonville, Tallahassee, and Pensacola.
On FOX, outside of the Dolphins game broadcast area, the rest of the state will have the Washington Commanders at the Dallas Cowboys game.
8:20 p.m. Eastern time slot - Sunday Night Football
The Indianapolis Colts at the Kansas City Chiefs will air on the national broadcast for Sunday Night Football.

Title: Pennsylvania asks for CDC measles help amid Kennedy dispute
Article_Text:
The Pennsylvania health department has requested emergency support from the CDC as it grapples with one of the country’s largest and most deadly measles outbreaks, though with certain terms, according to a document reviewed by Reuters on Thursday.
The request comes on condition that the federal agency recognize four measles-associated deaths reported by the state, raising the stakes in a dispute with the Trump administration.
The state’s measles outbreak has become the focus of a standoff between Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Gov. Josh Shapiro, a Democrat. Kennedy has cast doubt on whether deaths reported in U.S. measles outbreaks since he took office were due to the virus or another cause, and instructed the CDC not to include the Pennsylvania fatalities in a national tally.
Disease experts say the move represented highly unusual interference by a health secretary in the determination by state health officials and could minimize the risks of measles in the eyes of the public. Kennedy has accused Shapiro of politicizing the outbreak in his state and of failing to request federal help.
In a letter sent to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention director Erica Schwartz on Wednesday evening, reviewed by Reuters, Pennsylvania secretary of health Debra Bogen said the state had begun the process to request emergency assistance from the CDC, known as Epi-Aid.
“The CDC’s choice not to publicly recognize the deaths undermines our response,” Bogen wrote. “For this reason, if CDC is unable to transparently and accurately communicate information about those measles-associated deaths, the Department will respectfully rescind our request for a CDC Epi-Aid.”
The request from the state health department comes after it had resisted CDC help, arguing it had the outbreak under control.
In a statement, HHS spokesperson Grace Davis Jamison said CDC had not received Pennsylvania’s request through “normal channels,” and that federal outbreak assistance is a separate issue from the way CDC chooses to tabulate fatality data.
“CDC will not submit to political blackmail that conditions critical public health assistance,” said Jamison.
When the Pennsylvania health department announced the first two measles-associated fatalities on Aug. 25, the disease had sickened 393 people across 28 counties. Shapiro praised his health department’s efforts to vaccinate more people, and the state health department opted not to ask the CDC to send personnel to help on the ground.
Shapiro has criticized Kennedy, a longtime anti-vaccine activist who has promoted policies to reduce childhood immunization, for amplifying public fears about vaccines without scientific evidence. Kennedy and Schwartz have blamed Shapiro for not accepting their offers of Epi-Aid, a form of short-term CDC assistance during public health emergencies. The agency sends experts to the site of a disease outbreak, typically for one to three weeks, to provide additional support to state and local health departments.
Pennsylvania’s outbreak has since ballooned, growing to more than 700 confirmed cases across 37 counties and four measles-associated deaths, according to the state health department. It is the latest state to grapple with the worst US resurgence of measles in more than three decades, fueled by rising vaccine hesitancy, and coincides with President Donald Trump’s return to office in early 2025.
The disease’s spread in Pennsylvania is accelerating and could be 10 times larger than the official numbers, said Matthew Ferrari, director of the Center for Infectious Disease Dynamics at Penn State. Still, the state’s caution on CDC deployment is understandable, Ferrari said, as it could cause more problems if state and federal political leadership are not aligned on an issue as critical as what counts as a measles-related death.
The state “doesn’t want someone coming in, giving them advice and also telling them that the things that they’re experiencing are not as severe as they’re seeing with their own eyes,” he said. If the CDC ultimately doesn’t provide more assistance, he said, public health experts from other states could help.
One of the fatalities announced this week occurred in Mifflin County, which now has the second-highest number of cases in the state and is located over 100 miles from the outbreak’s initial epicenter in Lancaster County. At the same time, the pace of measles vaccinations provided by the state appears to be slowing, according to health department data.
In August, the health department administered over 3,500 doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine, which provides 97% protection against infection after two doses. For the first half of September, that number dropped to around 1,100 doses.

Title: Kennedy tells anti-vaccine activists they have a friend in Trump's White House
Article_Text:
Kennedy tells anti-vaccine activists they have a friend in Trump's White House
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. tells anti-vaccine activists from an organization he once chaired that they have a friend in the White House
WASHINGTON -- Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. gave the keynote address Thursday at a conference of an anti-vaccine activist group he once chaired, telling the hundreds in attendance that they had a friend in President Donald Trump's White House.
It was Kennedy's first time appearing at the Children's Health Defense conference since he became secretary. Kennedy took leave from the group when he launched his bid to become president in 2023, but his speech Thursday served as a sort of homecoming, offering him a platform from which to hail the administration's steps to scale back vaccine guidance and reassure the activists in attendance that he was working to turn their priorities into policy.
“Let me be clear: You have a strong and steadfast friend in the White House. We've accomplished in 19 months things that would have seemed unthinkable two years ago,” he said.
The speech, peppered with questions about long established vaccine safety, also highlighted how once fringe views on vaccines have been given a prominent pulpit under the Trump administration.
Kennedy boasted about the administration's moves to downsize the childhood vaccination schedule and reshape a key vaccine advisory board — steps that have since been halted by a judge.
Kennedy lauded Trump for pushing ahead with attempts to overhaul vaccine guidance, including an executive order last month calling for spacing out the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, against medical groups' recommendations.
That executive order and now Kennedy's keynote speech at the Children's Health Defense conference mark a pivot by the White House and the Department of Health and Human Services, who earlier this year had appeared to be moving beyond vaccine efforts and toward a less contentious agenda on healthy food ahead of November’s midterm elections. HHS promoted the speech on its social media channels.
Kennedy, a longtime anti-vaccine activist, chaired Children’s Health Defense for years. He served as the group’s chief legal counsel and expanded it. After becoming health secretary last year, Kennedy moved at a blistering pace to overhaul public health guidance and revamp long-held precedents in vaccine policymaking.
Critics, among them many of the country's top medical associations, have said the moves risk stoking vaccine hesitancy and sowing confusion among Americans who endured a crisis of trust in their public health agencies following the COVID-19 pandemic. That public confidence continues to erode.
“We have not taken vaccines away from anybody. We have preserved access. But we have started asking the questions that you and millions of American parents have been asking for years,” Kennedy told the group.
Mary Holland, the CEO of Children’s Health Defense, referred to Kennedy as “Bobby” and said the group has “gratitude beyond words” to the HHS secretary for “recognizing there are real consequential issues around childhood vaccinations.”
Kennedy's appearance Thursday comes as the country faces its worst year for measles since 1991 and has seen seven reported measles-associated deaths in the last two years — more than the combined total of reported deaths over the previous three decades.
Pennsylvania officials have reported four measles-associated deaths this year. None of the four were vaccinated, according to the state health department. When state officials last month announced the first two of those deaths, it ignited a public feud between Gov. Josh Shapiro and Kennedy.
Shapiro blasted Kennedy's appearance on the social media site X Thursday, saying Kennedy “chose to spend his time today addressing the premier vaccine-denial conference in America.”
Shapiro said the HHS secretary should have encouraged people to get vaccinated for measles, "yet he couldn’t bring himself to do it. Instead, he pushed a narrative that continues to stoke fear and mistrust.”
A representative from the White House did not respond to an Associated Press request for comment on Kennedy’s appearance at the event.
Following Kennedy onstage Thursday was Andrew Wakefield, an author of a since-discredited study that linked the MMR vaccine to autism, which has fueled the anti-vaccine movement even though it was retracted.
Widespread scientific consensus and decades of studies have firmly concluded there is no link between vaccines and autism.
Shaughnessy Naughton, founder of 314 Action, a group that recruits scientists to run for public office, said Kennedy's decision to give a speech at the conference shows “the lack of seriousness he brings to HHS.”
"With a deadly measles outbreak killing people in Pennsylvania, the best thing Kennedy can do for Americans is step aside.”
___
Stobbe contributed from New York.

Title: Penn State Wrestling To Visit Lehigh On December 6
Article_Text:
Penn State Wrestling To Visit Lehigh On December 6
Penn State wrestling’s slow reveal of its 2026-27 non-conference schedule continued on Thursday.
Lehigh revealed that it will continue its longtime in-state rivalry with Penn State on the road in Bethlehem on Sunday, December 6.
This will be the 112th all-time meeting between the Nittany Lions and Mountain Hawks, dating back to 1911. Excluding the 2020-21 season, which restricted schedules due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Penn State and Lehigh will compete for the 82nd consecutive season, dating back to 1934.
In those meetings, Penn State is 74-34-3 and has won the last 14, with Lehigh’s last victory coming in Cael Sanderson’s first dual meet as head coach on November 13, 2009.
While the Nittany Lions are the standardbearer for Pennsylvania wrestling, Lehigh has never been any slouch, routinely finishing ranked in InterMat’s yearly polls and routinely sending wrestlers to the NCAA Tournament.
Last season, after losing 36-6 at Rec Hall on December 6, 2025, they rolled through EIWA play, won big at the EIWA Championships, and placed 16th at the NCAA Championships in March. They sent six wrestlers to Cleveland, headlined by third-place finisher Luke Stanich, along with blood round participants Sheldon Seymour, Max Brignola, and Rylan Rogers.
Stanich will return as the headliner on the 2026-27 Mountain Hawks at 141 pounds and will likely start the season at No. 1 because Jesse Mendez graduated and national champion Sergio Vega of Oklahoma State bumped up a weight.
Could this be a blockbuster early-season dual opportunity for Masanosuke Ono in his first year of folkstyle? We’ll have to wait and see.
Penn State currently has 10 confirmed opponents for 2026-27 so far, but only two dates are known.
The Nittany Lions will host Northern Colorado on Friday, February 19, which is their only other confirmed non-conference bout. The eight opponents they’ll face in Big Ten play are locked in, but dates are to be determined.

Title: Giants' Harbaugh explains big move after Rams' controversial travel decision
Article_Text:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay has received criticism from numerous analysts and fans after his team arrived in Melbourne, Australia, roughly 28 hours before the kickoff of their season opener against the rival San Francisco 49ers, which the Rams lost to the tune of 27-7.
Thus, how first-year New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh is handling his team's trip out West for the upcoming "Monday Night Football" game at the Rams has raised some eyebrows among members of the NFL community.
Per Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News, the Giants are flying out on Saturday night rather than completing a Sunday trip for the Rams game. Harbaugh said he got the idea from when he worked under then-Philadelphia Eagles head coach Andy Reid from 1998 through the 2007 season.
"I think it’s just been good," Harbaugh said about such a plan. "We did it in Philadelphia all those years, too. You get a chance to get your clocks set. We go out late so the guys are up a little later on a travel night two days before. We try to get them ready to be at their peak at night. That’s kind of the idea. The same thing we did at home [for 'Sunday Night Football' in Week 1], but now it’s on the road."
The Giants are coming off a 28-20 prime-time win over the rival Dallas Cowboys on Sept. 13 that impressed Big Blue fans and outsiders. Meanwhile, the Rams "withered away" and seemingly wanted no part of having to participate in all that was associated with completing a meaningful game held in Australia. Giants starting left guard Jon Runyan Jr. seems to be a fan of Harbaugh's schedule.
"This is my first time doing it, and I guess it makes sense with a Monday night game. Why not? That’s a long almost six-hour flight out to LA," Runyan said on Wednesday. "We have a walkthrough practice that next day [Sunday]. It’ll feel good on the body; not just getting off a flight, pretty much having a dinner, going to sleep and [playing]. ...I feel like guys will take advantage of that first night we get there. And then we have that whole day [Sunday] with the practice, get some rest and recovery, and you got the whole day on Monday, too, to get your body going. I think it works out well and makes sense. West Coast Monday night game going out early. I think it’s a good thing."
Against the Cowboys, Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart completed 23-of-29 passes for 230 yards and three touchdowns. He also rushed for 54 yards on 11 carries. Dart echoed previous comments and indicated he fully supports whatever Harbaugh wants regarding the Giants' trip to California.
"I haven't really done this a lot, so I'm still trying to figure some of that stuff out," Dart said about leaving a day earlier, per the Giants' website. "But whatever Coach Harbs says, I think it's exactly what we should be doing. So, I've got the confidence that it's going to put us in the right situation to be acclimated and to be prepared for the game."
As of Thursday morning, DraftKings Sportsbook had the Giants as seven-point road underdogs for the Week 2 clash.

Title: Kennedy addresses anti-vaccine conference, says they have friend in Trump's White House
Article_Text:
U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. gave the keynote address Thursday at a conference of an anti-vaccine activist group he once chaired, telling the hundreds in attendance that they had a friend in U.S. President Donald Trump’s White House.
It was Kennedy’s first time appearing at the Children’s Health Defense conference since he became secretary. Kennedy took leave from the group when he launched his bid to become president in 2023, but his speech Thursday served as a sort of homecoming, offering him a platform from which to hail the administration’s steps to scale back vaccine guidance and reassure the activists in attendance that he was working to turn their priorities into policy.
“Let me be clear: You have a strong and steadfast friend in the White House. We’ve accomplished in 19 months things that would have seemed unthinkable two years ago,” he said.
First-ever GOP midterm convention this week could magnify the party’s perils
The speech, peppered with questions about long established vaccine safety, also highlighted how once fringe views on vaccines have been given a prominent pulpit under the Trump administration.
Kennedy boasted about the administration’s moves to downsize the childhood vaccination schedule and reshape a key vaccine advisory board – steps that have since been halted by a judge.
Kennedy lauded Trump for pushing ahead with attempts to overhaul vaccine guidance, including an executive order last month calling for spacing out the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, against medical groups’ recommendations.
That executive order and now Kennedy’s keynote speech at the Children’s Health Defense conference mark a pivot by the White House and the Department of Health and Human Services, who earlier this year had appeared to be moving beyond vaccine efforts and toward a less contentious agenda on healthy food ahead of November’s midterm elections. HHS promoted the speech on its social media channels.
Kennedy, a longtime anti-vaccine activist, chaired Children’s Health Defense for years. He served as the group’s chief legal counsel and expanded it. After becoming health secretary last year, Kennedy moved at a blistering pace to overhaul public health guidance and revamp long-held precedents in vaccine policymaking.
Critics, among them many of the country’s top medical associations, have said the moves risk stoking vaccine hesitancy and sowing confusion among Americans who endured a crisis of trust in their public health agencies following the COVID-19 pandemic. That public confidence continues to erode.
“We have not taken vaccines away from anybody. We have preserved access. But we have started asking the questions that you and millions of American parents have been asking for years,” Kennedy told the group.
Mary Holland, the CEO of Children’s Health Defense, referred to Kennedy as “Bobby” and said the group has “gratitude beyond words” to the HHS secretary for “recognizing there are real consequential issues around childhood vaccinations.”
Kennedy’s appearance Thursday comes as the country faces its worst year for measles since 1991 and has seen seven reported measles-associated deaths in the last two years – more than the combined total of reported deaths over the previous three decades.
Pennsylvania officials have reported four measles-associated deaths this year. None of the four were vaccinated, according to the state health department. When state officials last month announced the first two of those deaths, it ignited a public feud between Gov. Josh Shapiro and Kennedy.
Shapiro blasted Kennedy’s appearance on the social media site X Thursday, saying Kennedy “chose to spend his time today addressing the premier vaccine-denial conference in America.”
Shapiro said the HHS secretary should have encouraged people to get vaccinated for measles, “yet he couldn’t bring himself to do it. Instead, he pushed a narrative that continues to stoke fear and mistrust.”
A representative from the White House did not respond to an Associated Press request for comment on Kennedy’s appearance at the event.
Following Kennedy onstage Thursday was Andrew Wakefield, an author of a since-discredited study that linked the MMR vaccine to autism, which has fuelled the anti-vaccine movement even though it was retracted.
Widespread scientific consensus and decades of studies have firmly concluded there is no link between vaccines and autism.
Shaughnessy Naughton, founder of 314 Action, a group that recruits scientists to run for public office, said Kennedy’s decision to give a speech at the conference shows “the lack of seriousness he brings to HHS.”
“With a deadly measles outbreak killing people in Pennsylvania, the best thing Kennedy can do for Americans is step aside.”

Title: How the 2026 MLB Postseason is shaping up
Article_Text:
How the 2026 MLB Postseason is shaping up
UPDATED: 09/19/2026 2:36PM
MILWAUKEE (CBS 58) — The Major League Baseball postseason picture continues to take shape with just over a week remaining in the regular season.
Five teams — the Milwaukee Brewers, Los Angeles Dodgers, Tampa Bay Rays, New York Yankees and Atlanta Braves — have officially secured postseason berths.
Boston could become the sixth team to punch its ticket Saturday, while the American League West is completely deadlocked and several teams remain alive for the final AL Wild Card spot.
Meanwhile, Brewers fans still have plenty to scoreboard watch as Milwaukee attempts to hold off Los Angeles for the National League's No. 1 seed.
Here are four games to keep an eye on Saturday:
Red Sox at Rays — LIVE
Boston has an opportunity to officially secure its place in October.
The Red Sox enter Saturday 84-70 and comfortably holding the second AL Wild Card spot.
Boston can clinch a postseason berth with a win over Tampa Bay combined with either a Texas loss to Toronto or a Houston loss to Atlanta later Saturday.
The Rays have already clinched a playoff berth and enter Saturday 93-60 with a four-game advantage over the Yankees in the AL East.
Tampa Bay is also battling for one of the American League's two first-round byes.
Blue Jays at Rangers — 6:05 p.m.
The AL West could hardly be tighter.
Texas and Houston both enter Saturday 77-77 and tied for first place, though the Astros currently own the division lead because they hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Rangers.
Texas also remains directly in the AL Wild Card race.
The Rangers enter one game behind the Chicago White Sox for the final Wild Card spot, while Toronto is two games back.
Texas owns the tiebreaker over Toronto, making Saturday's matchup particularly important for both teams.
A Rangers loss, combined with a Boston win earlier in the afternoon, would also send the Red Sox to the postseason.
Braves at Astros — 6:10 p.m.
One night after Atlanta clinched a postseason berth, the Braves can continue moving closer to an NL East championship while Houston tries to maintain control of the AL West.
Atlanta enters Saturday 90-64 with a five-game lead over Philadelphia and a magic number of three to clinch the division.
Houston, meanwhile, is tied with Texas at 77-77 atop the AL West but holds the head-to-head tiebreaker.
The Astros would therefore win the division if the two teams ultimately finish the regular season with identical records.
Houston is also involved in Boston's clinching scenario. A Red Sox win combined with an Astros loss would secure a playoff berth for Boston.
Giants at Dodgers — 8:10 p.m.
Once again, this is the late game Brewers fans should keep an eye on.
Los Angeles enters Saturday 94-60 after beating San Francisco on Friday night, remaining two games behind Milwaukee for the best record in the National League.
The Brewers enter Saturday 96-58 and own the head-to-head tiebreaker against the Dodgers.
That means Los Angeles cannot simply finish tied with Milwaukee. The Dodgers would need to finish with a better record to claim the NL's No. 1 seed.
Milwaukee's magic number to secure a first-round bye is three, while the Brewers continue to close in on locking up the top seed and home-field advantage throughout the National League playoffs.
Every Brewers win and Dodgers loss over the final eight games pushes Milwaukee closer to securing that path through October.
What to watch
Saturday could bring another postseason clinch, but the biggest chaos remains in the American League.
Cleveland entered the day with a one-game lead over the White Sox in the AL Central, while Houston and Texas are tied atop the AL West. The White Sox, Rangers, Blue Jays and Orioles also remain separated by just three games in the fight for the final AL Wild Card spot.
In the National League, Atlanta is closing in on the NL East title, while the Cubs, Phillies and Padres all enter Saturday at 85-69 and tied in the standings as they battle for Wild Card seeding.
For Milwaukee, the objective is increasingly clear: keep winning and keep Los Angeles behind them.
With eight games remaining, the Brewers control their path to the National League's No. 1 seed.
UPDATED: 09/18/2026 2:11PM
MILWAUKEE (CBS 58) — With the Major League Baseball regular season nearing its finish, several postseason races remain wide open heading into Friday night.
Four teams — the Milwaukee Brewers, Los Angeles Dodgers, Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees — have already secured postseason berths, while the Brewers and Dodgers have clinched their respective divisions.
Plenty remains unsettled, particularly in the American League, where the AL Central is tied, the AL West is separated by one game and three teams sit within three games of the final Wild Card spot.
Here are four games to keep an eye on Friday night:
Athletics at Guardians — FINAL | ATH 3 CLE 5
Cleveland enters Friday tied with the Chicago White Sox atop the AL Central at 78-75, though Chicago currently holds the division lead because it owns the head-to-head tiebreaker.
That leaves the Guardians holding the third and final AL Wild Card spot entering the night.
Cleveland has a two-game advantage over both Texas and Toronto, with Baltimore three games back. That makes every game critical as the Guardians open a series at home against the Athletics.
Cleveland does not hold the tiebreaker against either Texas or Toronto, adding even more importance to maintaining its advantage in the standings.
Blue Jays at Rangers — FINAL | TOR 1 TEX 7
Few games Friday carry more direct postseason implications than Toronto's trip to Texas.
The Blue Jays and Rangers both enter at 76-77, two games behind Cleveland for the final AL Wild Card berth.
For Texas, there is another path to October still very much in play. The Rangers are only one game behind the Houston Astros in the AL West.
Texas also owns the tiebreaker over both Toronto and Cleveland, meaning a strong finish could quickly change the postseason picture.
A Rangers win combined with a Guardians loss would pull Texas within one game of the final Wild Card spot. It could also move the Rangers into a tie for the AL West lead if Houston loses later Friday night.
Braves at Astros — FINAL | ATL 6 HOU 2
Both teams have something significant on the line in Houston.
Atlanta enters Friday 89-64 and four games ahead of Philadelphia in the NL East. The Braves can officially punch their ticket to the postseason with a win over the Astros.
Atlanta would also clinch a playoff berth if Arizona loses to the Yankees later Friday night.
Houston, meanwhile, enters at 77-76 with a one-game lead over Texas in the AL West.
The Astros own the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Rangers, but with less than two weeks remaining, Houston has little room for error with Texas directly behind it.
Giants at Dodgers — FINAL | SF 2 LAD 8
Brewers fans may want to stay up for the final game of the night.
Los Angeles has already clinched the NL West but still has plenty to play for when it hosts San Francisco.
The Dodgers enter Friday 93-60, two games behind the Brewers for the best record in the National League.
Milwaukee also owns the season tiebreaker over Los Angeles, meaning the Dodgers would have to finish with a better record than the Brewers to take the NL's No. 1 seed.
The Brewers enter Friday with a magic number of seven to secure the top seed in the National League. A Dodgers loss would knock that number down by one, regardless of what Milwaukee does against Baltimore.
What to watch
The American League remains the biggest source of drama entering Friday.
Chicago and Cleveland are tied atop the AL Central, Houston leads Texas by only one game in the AL West, and Cleveland, Texas, Toronto and Baltimore are all separated by just three games in the race for the final Wild Card spot.
In the National League, Atlanta has an opportunity to become the fifth team to clinch a postseason berth, while Milwaukee and Los Angeles continue their battle for the league's top seed and home-field advantage through the National League playoffs.

The American League should command most of the attention Thursday night.
Cleveland leads Chicago by just a half-game in the AL Central, Houston and Texas enter the night tied atop the AL West, and the White Sox hold only a narrow advantage in the battle for the final Wild Card berth.
With several of those contenders playing at nearly the same time, the playoff picture could look considerably different by the end of the night.

Title: Knicks pause ticket sales after error led to high prices
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
18 Sep 2026, 01:35 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Brenden Willsch)
The New York Knicks halted ticket sales on Thursday after an internal error led to some sky-high prices.
The get-in price for tickets to the Knicks' season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers is $1,251, according to TicketData.com.
The team plans to roll out lower prices early next week.
'We are pausing Knicks individual ticket sales due to a mistake in our pricing,' Madison Square Garden Sports said in a statement. 'We are rolling back to last year's prices plus an average increase of 12%. We will restart sales with new prices shortly, and anyone who already purchased individual tickets will be refunded the difference.'
The Knicks, led by guard Jalen Brunson, are coming off their first NBA title in 53 years so a price increase was expected.
But when the Knicks opened up single-game tickets on Wednesday, the get-in price for the Oct. 20 opener against the 76ers at Madison Square Garden hit $1,363. The figure had spiked as high as $1,408 this week when single-game tickets were first made available to Knicks Fan First Chase cardholders on Monday.
'Our intention was never to overcharge our loyal fans, and we thank everyone for their support of the Knicks and their patience as we get this right,' MSG said.
The contest with the 76ers is highly anticipated after Philadelphia signed LeBron James and acquired Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics over the offseason to make for a powerhouse foursome with Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.
The average get-in price for the Knicks' 45 scheduled preseason and regular season home games is currently $262. That is more than double that of any other team, with tickets to get into Los Angeles Lakers home games averaging $130, followed by the Celtics at $99.
At the other end of the spectrum, the current average get-in price for Charlotte Hornets and Memphis Grizzlies home games both sit at just $23.
The Knicks won last year's title by beating the San Antonio Spurs in five games in the NBA Finals.
--Field Level Media

Title: Gov. Josh Shapiro speaks at AI conference in Pittsburgh
Article_Text:
Gov. Josh Shapiro gives keynote speech at AI Horizons conference in Pittsburgh
Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro spoke at Thursday's AI Horizons conference in Pittsburgh.
You can watch Gov. Shapiro's full speech in the video player above.
The conference brings together tech leaders, startups and innovators at Bakery Square to discuss the future of artificial intelligence and its impact on communities.
The AI Horizons conference
Joanna Doven, CEO of AI Strike Team and producer of AI Horizons, said the conversations over the next couple of days are focused not only on how AI can be used safely in daily life but also on sending a message to those leading AI innovation.
It was noted several times during the event that Pittsburgh is well-suited for this type of work, with the infrastructure to set an example for cities across the United States.
Panelists talked about concerns regarding AI taking over and the importance of setting guardrails, training people for an AI-driven future and earning the trust of the community.
Doven said the conversations surrounding AI are not going away and stressed that Pittsburgh is staying ahead of the curve.
“That the builders of serious AIs that are solving human problems, they are choosing to build in Pittsburgh, not Silicon Valley, because there is an underlying ethos that to build hard things, it takes some time, it takes humans at the wheel and it takes a certain culture of grit that only Pittsburgh has,” Doven said.
Mayor Corey O’Connor joined leaders from Ernst & Young and Nvidia to discuss how artificial intelligence could transform city services, including permitting, trash collection and pothole repairs.
"Coming and hearing what other technologies are available to streamline our services to enable us to put out public works individuals in different ways so we can put out a good product for our residents is really something that we have to be innovative with and think completely differently than we did in the past," O’Connor said.
During the discussion, leaders highlighted the importance of being intentional with AI implementation, including setting guardrails, training employees for an AI-driven future and earning the trust of the community.
It was said several times that Pittsburgh is in a prime position to lead the charge in AI innovation. O’Connor made it clear that the city would not use AI until there is a clear path for its application. In no world would they replace someone, but believes if it can make things easier for their employees, they want to hear it out.
The mayor also emphasized efforts to keep Pittsburgh in the spotlight as a leader in AI and as a city that supports business growth.
"For us to sell ourselves, we have to be ourselves, and that means if you are calling somebody from Pittsburgh, we are calling you back. We are going to be very aggressive in selling our region because we have to," O’Connor said.
Shapiro echoed a similar message and hopes top tech and government leaders can work together to find a way to use AI effectively and ethically.
"The leading companies in this space, and some who are here with us today, have openly talked about what could happen if this technology falls into the wrong hands, and how, more and more, their own hands can't fully guide it and shape it," Shapiro said. "The fear and confusion that everyday Americans have is understandable, and it needs to be addressed comprehensively with a focus on responsible, safe and ethical uses of this extraordinary technology."
Shapiro also voiced his criticism of House Speaker Mike Johnson for recessing at a time he believes lawmakers should be discussing AI's future.
Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to visit the United States, and Shapiro urged President Donald Trump to make artificial intelligence a top priority during their discussions.
"This should be among the top issues on President Trump's agenda for their visit. I, for one, hope that President Trump will leave the bluster and showmanship at the door," Shapiro said.
At the end of the first day of the summit, a hack-a-thon was announced to address housing in Allegheny County. Students who participate have the chance to win $30,000 in prizes.

Title: The Ninety Nine restaurant chain may be sold
Article_Text:
In this edition: Spot on the hot seat, Wayfair’s free space for startups, Roche lands in Allston
Jon here. At the Ninety Nine, it’s always the real deal. So will its current owner strike a good one for employees and regulars as it puts the New England icon up for sale?
If someone has been sending you this newsletter, it’s time to get your own copy. Sign up at globe.com/powerplay.
Featuring: Bill Foley, Joe Milano, Ryan Durkin, Enrique Colbert, Bruce Percelay, Rick Vanzura, Amanda McMaster, Bob Luz, Jim Kiley, Kevin Stone, Manu Chakravarthy, Bill Tyree, Spot, and more.
Several Ninety Nine restaurant managers took to the mound at Fenway Park for the ceremonial first pitch on Sept. 9 — an annual tradition known as “99 Night” to honor employees’ charity work.
By coincidence, word emerged earlier that day that Ninety Nine’s sister chain, O’Charley’s, is shutting down completely.
One restaurant chain is thriving. The other closing. What to make of it? All signs point one way: that a sale of Ninety Nine, a beloved New England fixture for decades, is in the works.
What it means for the Woburn-based restaurant group remains to be seen. But untethering Ninety Nine from the failing O’Charley’s can’t hurt, and maybe even could help.
Executives at Cannae Holdings, a quirky public company that’s part of Las Vegas billionaire Bill Foley’s constellation of businesses, have been telling analysts for months that they’re engaged in a “strategic review” of Cannae’s remaining two restaurant chains. (How quirky? Cannae’s other holdings include football clubs and a slug of SpaceX stock.)
O’Charley’s, by far the worse performer of the two, didn’t survive this “strategic review.” Chief executive Ryan Caswell has promised investors there would be sale proceeds. Left unsaid: from selling Ninety Nine.
No matter how you prefer your chicken wings, a strange new chapter is unfolding for the business that Charlie Doe started 74 years ago, on State Street in downtown Boston. The “99″ refers to the first location’s street address; its country-and-western-esque logo is a throwback to the horseshoe that Doe’s wife hung there for good luck.
Members of the Doe family built Ninety Nine into a solid regional casual dining business before reaching a deal to sell it to Nashville-based O’Charley’s in 2002. Along the way, they fostered a culture around employee retention and giving back to the community. Under out-of-state ownership, Ninety Nine had considerable autonomy, at least to start. It became known for its Red Sox sponsorship, a partnership that continues to this day, notably with the famous kids-eat-free promotion on days following Sox wins.
Ninety Nine succeeded when it stuck to its core New England market, tapping into regional pride, and family-friendly pub menu (not to mention the free popcorn). A push into Philadelphia didn’t work. Neither did a foray into higher-end entrees. The restaurant count has fallen back slightly from its peak, and now appears stable at 93 locations and 4,000-plus employees. Sales at locations open at least a year fell only 3 percent in the first six months of 2026, compared to 13 percent for O’Charley’s.
Jim Kiley, a former regional vice president who left about three years ago, says Ninety Nine largely recovered from the COVID-19 shutdowns that hammered the industry, unlike O’Charley’s. Kiley says toward the end of his tenure, top Ninety Nine managers were hamstrung by corporate edicts. He says odds are good they’ll find more freedom under a new owner.
“No matter who picks them up, they have to be better off than they were before,” said Bob Luz, the prior Massachusetts Restaurant Association CEO, and former O’Charley’s/Ninety Nine chief human resources officer. “Someone needs to come in and reinvest in it. ... You’re not picking up something that’s totally broken. It just needs a little bit of love.”
The Cannae CEO hinted he had a buyer lined up, telling investors last month that more time was needed to secure financing. And this week, a Ninety Nine spokesperson said decisions about O’Charley’s have no impact on Ninety Nine, while Ninety Nine will continue to focus on its “loyal guests in New England” for many more years to come regardless of any ownership change.
Rick Vanzura, a veteran restaurant exec who now is president of local startup GrowthFactor, says the future buyer is more likely a private equity firm than a restaurant operator, given the challenges the industry faces and the chain’s specific geographic focus, though the cash flow might attract a family office instead. Vanzura hopes a more committed owner will improve the group’s prospects.
“They have a good reputation historically, but I assume now they’re a little rudderless,” Vanzura said. “I can think of few circumstances where being owned by someone who believes in you isn’t better than being owned by someone who wants to sell you.”
Wishful thinking? While private equity isn’t inherently bad, we all know stories about PE firms that take on too much debt and then strip-mine their portfolios’ profits and assets.
That said, Cannae is clearly eager to deal, so a buyer probably won’t need to borrow too much money. Charlie Doe’s good-luck charm might just pay off after all.
SHIRLEY’S TAKE
HEARD AROUND TOWN
GOOD DOG, BAD DEAL?
Dozens are expected to show up Saturday outside the Museum of Science – where Boston Dynamics’ Spot is on exhibit – to protest potential sales of the robotic dog to ICE. The agency is seeking to purchase up to $2 million worth of “Spot” robots to support law enforcement operations. Members of the De-ICE Citizens Bank Coalition, which successfully pressured Citizens to stop providing financing for two for-profit prison companies used by ICE, sent an Aug. 31 letter to Boston Dynamics interim CEO Amanda McMaster raising concerns about how ICE’s Spot deal could violate the company’s own ethics policies. “There is every reason to worry that ICE will use your products in ways you do not intend and will show similar obstructiveness if they are reminded what acceptable uses are,” the group wrote.
MEET THE NEW BOSS
There’s a new boss on the way for financial services firm Brown Brothers Harriman, and this one will be primarily based in New York as well – not Boston – even though we have BBH’s largest office. Today, BBH announced it is promoting its chief financial officer, Kevin Stone, to the chief executive role, to take over for managing partner Bill Tyree on Jan. 1; Tyree is retiring after more than 40 years with the 6,000-person firm. Stone is also a BBH vet, having joined the business in 1992. Roughly twice as many people work at BBH’s Boston office, in the former New England Telephone and Telegraph tower on Franklin Street, as in the firm’s 750-person office in New York. BBH specializes in two lines of work: Capital Partners (wealth management, private equity, and corporate banking) and Investor Services (providing services to big fund managers). It was the latter division that State Street tried to buy but eventually gave up amid an unexpectedly protracted antitrust review in 2022.
ROCHE ARRIVES IN ALLSTON
Can Harvard build its own version of what MIT has done with Kendall Square? It’s the question that’s been hanging over Allston for years, as Harvard looks to attract commercial development to its vast real estate next to its business school. Today marks an important milestone in that quest: Roche celebrates a ribbon-cutting for its 100,000-square-foot “Roche Genentech Innovation Center” (otherwise known by the awkward acronym of RGIC). That’s where the company will focus on cardiovascular, renal and metabolic research along with using AI to accelerate drug discoveries. Roche is the first big life sciences tenant to land at the newly opened Enterprise Research Campus, so it makes sense Governor Maura Healey and Boston Mayor Michelle Wu would be on hand. Also expected to attend: Fritz Bittenbender, head of public affairs at Roche’s Genentech division, and Manu Chakravarthy, the head of Roche’s new Boston site.
YOUR TURN
In Tuesday’s edition, we asked readers to weigh in on Mayor Michelle Wu’s willingness to give developers $100 million in tax breaks to jumpstart housing. Gary S. writes: “This should have been done long ago and at a much higher level … Your article sounds like a congratulatory one; better you offer suggestions to do more.” Meanwhile, John G. thinks developers should hold out for more. “Wu only bargains when her back is against the wall, and her image starts to suffer. The developers should keep playing hardball with Wu.” Then there’s Bruce Percelay, who owns and manages apartment buildings in Boston, looking for his subsidy: “Those who have existing buildings will also need tax relief as it will put those who took risks early on at a competitive disadvantage.”
ONE MORE THING
Larry Edelman joins Shirley in the Globe podcast studio to talk more about how the Massachusetts economy lost its mojo and how we get it back. (Yes, Larry made the long trip in from the Adirondacks.) Listen here and wherever you get your podcasts.
THANKS FOR READING POWER PLAY.
Today’s edition was written by Jon Chesto and Shirley Leung, edited by Aaron Pressman, and produced by Dana Gerber.
Have a question for the team? Email us at powerplay@globe.com.
Delivered Tuesday and Thursday.
Jon Chesto can be reached at jon.chesto@globe.com. Follow him @jonchesto. Shirley Leung is a Business columnist. She can be reached at shirley.leung@globe.com.

Title: Breakfast briefing: Financial market relief
Article_Text:
Here's our summary of key economic events overnight that affect New Zealand, with news it seems yesterday's unanimous Fed decision to prioritise the inflation fight has financial markets reassured. The US Treasury yields have pulled back from their highs, although still at Tuesday's high level.
One thing millions are watching is whether US mortgage rates will hit 7% again. They haven't quite yet but it is close. Not only are new home and refinance borrowers affected, the house building industry and all that it supports are anxious as well.
But first in the US today, their weekly initial jobless claims fell last week and by more than expected and by more than seasonal factors would have indicated. There are now 1.58 mln people on these benefits, also a notable fall as the much tighter qualification rules start to bit hard now.
US housing starts fell and to their slowest pace since 2019, with the exceptions of the sharp and unusual May dip, and the pandemic. That was matched by low building consent levels, so the easing off in this homebuilding sector will continue.
The regional Philly Fed factory survey for the important Pennsylvanian rust belt region was expected to fall in September from August and it did, but not by as much as expected. New orders and shipments remained elevated, while the employment index declined but stayed positive, signaling continued job growth. Both input and output price indicators moved higher and at a faster pace.
US pending home sales were down -4.7% in August from a year ago, but at least they did manager to level-peg from July.
There was a US 10 year TIPS bond auction overnight which delivered a median yield of 2.58% (high 2.65%), which is a notable rise from the 2.37% at the prior equivalent event a month ago. Although not as dramatic as the -17% fall off in demand for yesterday's 20 year bond, this auction attracted lower demand as well, -12% less.
And we should probably note that Chinese president Xi will be visiting the US next week and there is a frenzy of advanced negotiations underway in preparation so that both he and Trump can announce something 'substantial' and worth the visit. What will be interesting will be the moves after the event glad-handling.
In Canada, their producer prices rose sharply again, up +13.5% from a year ago in August, driven of course by high fuel costs. On the same basis their diesel is up +75% and petrol up +42%. Both rose notably from July as well.
Singapore's electronics sector had a boom month in August helping power the country's non-oil exports to a +46% gain from the same month a year earlier. That was up very sharply from a downwardly revised +24.1% rise in July and far above forecasts of +35%. It was the twelfth straight month of expansion and the strongest growth since October 1988. The US was a smaller customer in August than July. But every other major country was a much larger customer (other than the EU).(Meanwhile their imports rose +39% but that includes oil.)
Overnight the Bank of England reviewed their policy rate and left it unchanged at 3.75%. Three of their nine voters wanted a rise. That kept their no-change streak of 2026 intact. Taiwan reviewed its 2.0% policy rate, also keeping it unchanged. And later today the more important Bank of Japan review is expected to announce a +25 bps hike to 1.25%.
In Australia, they released updated population data yesterday. This is a hot topic politically. Their population grew by +1.4% in the 12 months to March 2026, now 27.9 million people. That's 392,700 more than the same time in 2025. The natural increase was +100,000 and the net migration increase was +292,100 (and down from +309,500 in the previous year). The state with the biggest increase was Victoria (+109,500); the state with the fastest increase was Western Australia (+2.1%).
Global container freight rates have stayed very high but are in fact little-changed from last week at this time. From a year ago they are up +135% however. Within the recent no-change, rates from China to Europe were down about -5% while rates from China to the US rose about +5%. Bulk cargo rates fell -8% in the past week, but are also historically high still and up +55% from a year ago.
The UST 10yr yield is now just on 4.94%, down -7 bps from yesterday. The 30 year yield is at 5.29%, also down -6 bps. The key 2-10 yield curve is now at +26 bps (down -8 bps). Their 1-5 curve is now at +42 bps (-2 bps) and the 3 mth-10yr curve is at +109 bps (-2 bps). The China 10 year bond rate is little-changed at 1.69%. The Japanese 10 year bond yield is now at 3.00%, unchanged. The Australian 10 year bond yield starts today at 5.27%, down -4 bps from yesterday. The NZ Government 10 year bond rate is now at 5.03%, down -1 bp.
Wall Street is rising today, up +1.2% in Thursday trade on the S&P500, and up +1.6% on the Nasdaq. Overnight, European markets were firmer between Lindon's +1.2% rise and Paris's +0.6%. Yesterday Tokyo ended up +0.3%. Hong Kong was down -0.4% and Shanghai eased similarly. Singapore was up +0.4%. The ASX ended its Thursday trade up +0.1%. And the NZX50 rose a full +1.0% again.
The price of gold was at US$4360/oz, and recovering +US$111 from yesterday. Silver is at just over US$65.50/oz and up +US$2.50/oz.
Oil prices have eased -50 USc to US$102/bbl in the US, while the international Brent price is little-changed at US$104.50/bbl. Hormuz transits are still low today with just seven ships exiting over the past 24 hours, two tankers escorted (2 dark with transponders off) and eight entering for new loads (4 dark). The Red Sea activity is now only about 15 each way at the Yemen chokepoint in a sudden shift
The Kiwi dollar is down -30 bps from yesterday, now at 57.3 USc. Against the Aussie we are down -20 bps at 80.6 AUc. Against the euro we are unchanged at just on 49.9 euro cents. That all means our TWI-5 starts today at just under 60.8, down -20 bps and still at a six-week low.
The bitcoin price starts today at US$76,622 and up +1.5% from yesterday. Volatility over the past 24 hours has been modest again at just over +/-1.0%.

Title: ICE is laying off agents hired during its rapid expansion after discovering discrepancies in their backgrounds
Article_Text:
ICE is laying off agents hired during its rapid expansion after discovering discrepancies in their backgrounds
A ‘Washington Post’ investigation reveals that the agency hired thousands of officers with incomplete background checks, while a whistleblower warned of an unprecedented lowering of hiring standards
Joseph Moore had spent years trying to build a career in law enforcement. A former Marine reservist and father of two, the 38-year-old finally landed a job as a deportation officer with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in 2025. Less than a year later, the agency decided to fire him. And just hours after going to an ICE office in Philadelphia to learn about his employment status, Moore died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, according to police.
His case was part of an internal review of some of the thousands of officers hired during ICE’s rapid expansion to increase migrant arrests and deportations. Months after bringing in about 12,000 new officers, the agency has begun firing some of them after identifying problems in their backgrounds or reports of inadequate performance, according to an investigation by the Washington Post.
Moore had previously worked for police departments in Pennsylvania and as a criminal investigator with the Internal Revenue Service, but he had been fired from both jobs. In May 2026, seven months after joining ICE, the agency began questioning his suitability because of those employment records. Moore challenged the decision and continued working for another three months.
On August 21, he was involved in an accident with an official vehicle that left him with a concussion and several broken bones. Days later, the agency informed him that he would be fired. On August 28, he went to the ICE office in Philadelphia carrying his service weapon. Local police said officers attempted to intervene before Moore shot himself.
His family has challenged the official account and says Moore was speaking by phone with an ICE official who was trying to calm the situation. Police, meanwhile, said none of the officers fired their weapons and that Moore was the one who drew his gun.
The episode came amid a review of hiring carried out during one of the largest expansions in ICE’s recent history. The strategy, fueled by billions of dollars approved by Congress, called for increasing the agency’s workforce from approximately 10,000 to 22,000 officers. To attract candidates, the agency offered signing bonuses of up to $50,000 and received more than 220,000 applications. In January, it announced that it had hired 12,000 new officers in less than a year.
But the pace of hiring had raised internal concerns about the quality of background checks. A supervisor in ICE’s Office of Professional Responsibility, who oversaw background investigations, warned in August 2025 that the agency’s human resources staff was making final job offers before preliminary checks had been completed.
The official said some candidates had been allowed to begin training before fingerprint, identity, and credit checks had been completed. In a memo to the Department of Homeland Security’s Office of Inspector General, the whistleblower warned of an “unprecedented lowering of standards” and argued that the rush was sidelining basic measures designed to mitigate risks.
The complaint also said the failures could increase ICE’s vulnerability to insider threats, infiltration, and foreign influence. The supervisor called for the practices to be suspended, recent hires to be reviewed, and potential security risks to be identified.
Nevertheless, the expansion continued despite those warnings. The agency cut weeks of basic training and allowed some candidates with previous law enforcement experience to bypass its training academy. Two former officers interviewed by the Washington Post described onboarding processes conducted primarily by email and online courses, without in-person interviews.
The pressure on ICE facilities was also evident. One former officer said his office went from bringing in one or two new employees at a time to receiving as many as 60, resulting in a shortage of desks and workspace.
Concerns about the hiring process have grown following other incidents. In July, the government announced that it would review ICE’s screening procedures after an immigrant was fatally shot in Maine by an officer hired during the agency’s major expansion, despite having a history of domestic violence, according to his family and people close to him. He had also been accused of assaulting several women. In addition, an Associated Press investigation found that some new officers had serious financial problems, allegations of misconduct, and troubled employment histories.
ICE has defended its procedures and said it rigorously applies its background-check requirements. The agency has also said that firings are nothing new and that personnel decisions are made when employees fail to meet established requirements.

Title: Brendan Gleeson, Jennifer Jason Leigh Among 5 Cast In FX's 'Far Cry'
Article_Text:
FX‘s anthology series Far Cry has added Brendan Gleeson, Jennifer Jason Leigh, Hamish Linklater, Sam Spruell and Jamie Demetriou to its cast.
They join the previously announced Rob Mac, Lizzy Caplan and Steve Buscemi in the cast of the series based on Ubisoft’s global hit video game franchise.
Each season of the Noah Hawley and Mac series will retain Far Cry’s signature standalone storytelling format, with each season set in a new setting and following a new cast of characters. Details regarding the plot of Season 1 are under wraps.
Six game releases, from 2004 to 2021, have been released as part of the franchise, with an additional seven spinoffs and expansions. The games are known for the exhilaration of the first-person shootouts, organic open-world playgrounds, unique stories, and memorable antagonists.
Watch on Deadline
FX’s Far Cry is executive produced by Hawley, who created FX’s anthology series Fargo and Alien: Earth for TV through his 26 Keys production banner, and Rob Mac, creator of It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia and Executive Producer of Welcome to Wrexham through his production banner More Better Productions. In addition to Mac and Hawley, the series is executive produced by Simon Emanuel, Emilia Serrano for 26 Keys, Nicholas Frenkel for 3 Arts, Monica Macer, Peter Calloway, John Campisi, Gerard Guillemot, Margaret Boykin, and Austin Dill for Ubisoft Film & Television. The series will be produced by FX Productions.
Gleeson is represented by CAA and Principal Entertainment. Leigh is represented by CAA and Untitled Entertainment. Linklater is represented by Untitled Entertainment, Gersh, and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole. Spruell is represented by Lou Coulson Associates and Luber Roklin Entertainment. Demetriou is represented by United Agents, CAA, and Multitude Media.
