Title: Philadelphia Ganesh Festival brings 2,000 Indian Americans
Article_Text:
For Indian American families raising children in the United States, keeping cultural traditions alive can often happen through moments that bring generations together.
In Greater Philadelphia, the annual Ganesh Festival at Bharatiya Temple is becoming one such gathering.
Around 2,000 devotees and community members from the region and neighboring states took part in the festival’s opening celebrations on Sept. 14, as families gathered for the Ganesh procession, prayers, devotional activities, cultural programs and Maha Prasad.
The 11-day celebration, which runs through Sept. 25, is not only bringing devotees together for religious observances. It is also creating a space where Indian American parents and grandparents can introduce children and grandchildren raised in the United States to the traditions, stories, music, dance and spiritual practices they grew up with in India.
For the growing Indian American community in the Philadelphia region, the festival is increasingly becoming a meeting point between generations and a way to experience Indian culture within the American community.
The celebrations began Sept. 14 with a traditional procession and religious ceremonies dedicated to Lord Ganesha. Families participated in prayers and devotional activities before coming together for Maha Prasad.
READ: Dallas Telugu organization to host large Telangana Bonalu festival in Frisco (July 23, 2026)
Each evening through Sept. 25, the festival is featuring religious, cultural or devotional programming, bringing different aspects of Indian traditions to the community.
One of the highlights of the opening day was “Krishna… Ek Anokha Nrityavishkar,” a classical dance-drama presented by Guru Sonia Parchure and her group.
The production portrayed the divine life and spiritual journey of Lord Krishna through Kathak, abhinaya, music, choreography and storytelling. For families attending the festival, the performance offered another way to connect younger generations with Indian classical arts and stories rooted in the country’s cultural and spiritual heritage.
Another cultural program followed on Sept. 15, continuing the series of evening events featuring music, dance, devotion and Indian cultural expression.
The festival’s organizers are also seeing the impact of the community’s growing participation. Expanded parking facilities at Bharatiya Temple have allowed the venue to accommodate more devotees and visitors as attendance continues to increase.
But beyond the numbers, the festival reflects a broader question faced by many Indian American families: how to keep cultural connections strong when children are growing up far from the places where their parents and grandparents grew up.
For some families, religious and cultural festivals provide an opportunity to make those traditions part of everyday life for younger generations rather than limiting them to stories about India or family memories.
Dr. Ravi Murarka, a longtime member of the Greater Philadelphia Indian-American community, said celebrations such as the Philadelphia Ganesh Festival can help families pass those traditions and values to their children and grandchildren.
“For families who have made America their home, festivals like this give us an opportunity to introduce our children and grandchildren to the traditions, values, devotion, and cultural heritage with which many of us grew up in India,” Dr. Murarka said. “It is especially meaningful to see younger generations participating and learning about their roots while celebrating together as one community.”
The festival brings those traditions into a community setting through puja, processions, devotional music, classical dance, cultural performances and Maha Prasad.
READ: Diwali: The lamp within us all (October 19, 2025)
For children and young adults who were born or raised in the United States, participating in these activities can offer a direct experience of Indian customs and traditions that their parents and grandparents may have practiced while growing up in India.
The festival also creates opportunities for multiple generations of the same family to participate together. Grandparents can share familiar traditions with grandchildren, while parents can introduce their children to Indian spiritual practices and cultural expressions in an environment surrounded by other Indian American families.
The cultural programs are an important part of that experience. Classical dance, music and storytelling allow younger members of the community to encounter Indian traditions in ways that extend beyond religious ceremonies.
The growing participation has also brought Indian American families from outside the immediate Philadelphia area to Bharatiya Temple, with devotees and visitors traveling from neighboring states to join the celebrations.
As the Indian American population continues to establish communities across the United States, festivals such as this have become occasions not only for worship but also for cultural exchange, family gatherings and community building.
At Bharatiya Temple, the Philadelphia Ganesh Festival is bringing those elements together over 11 days, giving families an opportunity to celebrate Lord Ganesha while also creating space for younger generations to experience the traditions their families brought with them from India.
The celebrations will continue through Sept. 25 with daily religious activities and cultural programs, bringing together Indian American families across the Greater Philadelphia region through devotion, music, dance, tradition and community.

Title: Kennedy tells anti-vaccine activists they have a friend in Trump's White House
Article_Text:
Kennedy tells anti-vaccine activists they have a friend in Trump's White House
WASHINGTON (AP) — Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. gave the keynote address Thursday at a conference of an anti-vaccine activist group he once chaired, telling the hundreds in attendance that they had a friend in President Donald Trump's White House.
It was Kennedy's first time appearing at the Children's Health Defense conference since he became secretary. Kennedy took leave from the group when he launched his bid to become president in 2023, but his speech Thursday served as a sort of homecoming, offering him a platform from which to hail the administration's steps to scale back vaccine guidance and reassure the activists in attendance that he was working to turn their priorities into policy.
“Let me be clear: You have a strong and steadfast friend in the White House. We've accomplished in 19 months things that would have seemed unthinkable two years ago,” he said.
The speech, peppered with questions about long established vaccine safety, also highlighted how once fringe views on vaccines have been given a prominent pulpit under the Trump administration.
Kennedy boasted about the administration's moves to downsize the childhood vaccination schedule and reshape a key vaccine advisory board — steps that have since been halted by a judge.
Kennedy lauded Trump for pushing ahead with attempts to overhaul vaccine guidance, including an executive order last month calling for spacing out the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, against medical groups' recommendations.
That executive order and now Kennedy's keynote speech at the Children's Health Defense conference mark a pivot by the White House and the Department of Health and Human Services, who earlier this year had appeared to be moving beyond vaccine efforts and toward a less contentious agenda on healthy food ahead of November’s midterm elections. HHS promoted the speech on its social media channels.
Kennedy, a longtime anti-vaccine activist, chaired Children’s Health Defense for years. He served as the group’s chief legal counsel and expanded it. After becoming health secretary last year, Kennedy moved at a blistering pace to overhaul public health guidance and revamp long-held precedents in vaccine policymaking.
Critics, among them many of the country's top medical associations, have said the moves risk stoking vaccine hesitancy and sowing confusion among Americans who endured a crisis of trust in their public health agencies following the COVID-19 pandemic. That public confidence continues to erode.
“We have not taken vaccines away from anybody. We have preserved access. But we have started asking the questions that you and millions of American parents have been asking for years,” Kennedy told the group.
Mary Holland, the CEO of Children’s Health Defense, referred to Kennedy as “Bobby” and said the group has “gratitude beyond words” to the HHS secretary for “recognizing there are real consequential issues around childhood vaccinations.”
Advertisement
Kennedy's appearance Thursday comes as the country faces its worst year for measles since 1991 and has seen seven reported measles-associated deaths in the last two years — more than the combined total of reported deaths over the previous three decades.
Pennsylvania officials have reported four measles-associated deaths this year. None of the four were vaccinated, according to the state health department. When state officials last month announced the first two of those deaths, it ignited a public feud between Gov. Josh Shapiro and Kennedy.
Shapiro blasted Kennedy's appearance on the social media site X Thursday, saying Kennedy “chose to spend his time today addressing the premier vaccine-denial conference in America.”
Shapiro said the HHS secretary should have encouraged people to get vaccinated for measles, "yet he couldn’t bring himself to do it. Instead, he pushed a narrative that continues to stoke fear and mistrust.”
A representative from the White House did not respond to an Associated Press request for comment on Kennedy’s appearance at the event.
Following Kennedy onstage Thursday was Andrew Wakefield, an author of a since-discredited study that linked the MMR vaccine to autism, which has fueled the anti-vaccine movement even though it was retracted.
Widespread scientific consensus and decades of studies have firmly concluded there is no link between vaccines and autism.
Shaughnessy Naughton, founder of 314 Action, a group that recruits scientists to run for public office, said Kennedy's decision to give a speech at the conference shows “the lack of seriousness he brings to HHS.”
"With a deadly measles outbreak killing people in Pennsylvania, the best thing Kennedy can do for Americans is step aside.”
___
Stobbe contributed from New York.

Title: AG Rob Bonta Says Paramount's California Exit Is David Ellison's Choice
Article_Text:
“We, respectfully, didn’t think that the United States DOJ did an adequate review, and we thought we needed to step in to make sure we were protecting consumers,” California AG Rob Bonta said of a lawsuit that’s rocking Hollywood after 12 attorneys general sued to block Paramount’s merger with Warner Bros. Discovery.
He was dinging the Department of Justice, which blessed the deal in June. “When we looked at, it was and continues to be, a black-and-white, bread-and-butter case. We looked at the facts. We looked at the law. We did our own independent assessment of the law, the facts, and we decided that there was an antitrust violation in three separate markets we set forth in our complaint,” he told The Atlantic Festival in New York on a panel of state attorneys general.
“We thought we needed to step in to make sure we were protecting consumers who are paying satellite bills and cable bills, consumers who are trying to enjoy one of the joys of life and go to the movies, and make sure that those costs aren’t raised, make sure that jobs are protected, make sure that those choices are in competition in the marketplace,” he said, appearing alongside New Hampshire AG John Formella and Pennsylvania AG David Sunday. They discussed how attorneys general have increasingly stepped up in antitrust and consumer protection fights across sectors with recent high-profile case against Live Nation-Ticketmaster, Nexstar-Tegna and Meta.
Watch on Deadline
RELATED: Parties Lay Out Key Discovery And Other Dates For Pending Paramount-WBD Antitrust Trial
The Paramount-WBD suit is set for trial in March. The AGs secured a temporary restraining order early on, and Paramount agreed to delay closing the deal until next summer. The court has ordered two days of settlement talks in October, but the sides are far apart. Absent an agreement, Ellison this week escalated threats to pull Paramount out of California. It’s not clear to where. Nashville felt like a front-runner for a bit, but Texas might be gaining. Ellison has said he’d of course prefer to stay in California.
“There have been threats. Those aren’t new — the continued threats to leave the state of California. I can’t comment on what a company decides to do, especially a company that has professed a commitment to Hollywood and to California. If they make that choice to leave, that is their choice and their choice alone. They own it. It lies at their feet.,” Bonta said.
RELATED: The ParaBros Backlash: Threats To Leave L.A. & An AG Who Won’t Back Down Divide Hollywood
“We have a job to enforce the law without fear, without favor, and at the same time, we are always open to coming to the table if it is in good faith and sincere, and we will always explore an opportunity to get the results that we want based on our evaluation of the case at the table.”
Bonta is looking for major concessions said to include selling WBD’s cable networks and keeping the operations of the two studios separate. Ellison is likely trying to calculate what compromises he can afford. He has promised $6 billion in synergies. The combined company would have about $80 billion in debt to service.
RELATED: Could Cable TV, That Vestige Of Bygone Media Glory, Undo The Paramount-WBD Merger?
Asked about Paramount’s insistence that plaintiffs post a $1.88 billion bond, Bonta said: “What I think that is they don’t have any right to that. In our view. I think that’s buyer’s remorse. … There was no part of the agreement [with the court] that involved the states posting a bond.”
The judge will rule on a bond at a Septmber 24 hearing.
“They’re trying to rewrite an agreement, a commitment, a promise that they already made, and we feel very confident going into a hearing,” Bonta added. “The judge will decide.”
The bond would cover a ticking fee Par agreed to pay Warner as a term of the merger — $7 million-a-day starting October 1 if the merger had not closed. That would come to $1.88 billion by early June. Either side can walk away at that point. Paramount would owe WBD a $7 billion termination fee in that case instead of the ticking fee.
The DOJ filed a brief to the case docket this week supporting Paramount’s right to a bond. Paramount insists it is statutorily entitled to a bond. It has defended the merger, announced in February, as good for the entertainment industry and committed to making 30 films a year between the two studios.
RELATED: Paramount CEO David Ellison Complains About “Needless Costs” Of State AGs’ Antitrust Suit
Terrible shame. Paramount’s departure will further cement California’s anti-business reputation. Can’t blame Paramount for wanting out.
Well, Mr. Bonta, respectfully, who is paying for your little jaunt to the East Coast to speak on a panel at The Atlantic Festival in New York? Maybe be a little concerned about your taxpayers, who undoubtedly are paying for your trip one way or another. How much did this cost? Why is every California politician always speaking from places OTHER than California? Ya know, the state they allegedly represent? Spare us your “for the consumers” rhetoric. This is about Ego and Headlines. You can do your job from your office. No need to grandstand on the other side of the country.
Yes! Newsom started debating Florida governor DeSantis years ago. Do all these politicians think California is in such a great place that they can bounce around the country? Please do your job and fix this state.
It is a political case! Why only 12 Democrat states, not all 50 states? Why all 70 countries including US approved the deal? Bonta is doing the job to push jobs out of California!
CA could be the most glorious state in the union. For the love of God, is there anyone competent out there, waiting to step up? Any sane moderate? Any sane liberal? Anyone who is actually focused on fixing this state? If they leave, we are staring down into the abyss, folks. This town will not recover. Not for a very long time. I don’t know anyone who wants this merger. But this is where we are. And our state is suffering. Bonta is not a serious person. God, politics have ruined every aspect of our lives. And to top it off, we’ve got runaway AI, about to decimate God only knows what. Sane leadership, willing to deal with what is. That’s all.
My sentiments exactly!
Paramount leaving is the least of our problems, you should look into what’s going on with the Colorado River.
The same was said when the defense industry left for the most part. The city survived. It will survive this. California is booming. If you actually lived here you’d know that.
You’re obviously not a real person. Bot.
CA is not booming, quite the opposite. This state is a cesspool and only getting worse.
California is booming? Are you insane?
Are you a bot? I’ve lived here for over thirty years. I’ve put my children through schools, then college here. I love this state. But we have to be real, and acknowledge our city (and state) are in trouble. In April was daughter was the victim of a home invasion. We need to get a handle on our city, and try and build back our restaurants, our parks, our infrastructure. My best friend lost his restaurant in Santa Monica recently. His entire life savings wrapped up in the dream of being able to serve the community he loves.
I am so sorry about your friend. I was born and raised here, And it’s so disturbing to learn of fellow citizens diminish the very real problems we have
California is booming if you only look at the counties from San Francisco to San Jose. Do you think LA is booming? The Central Valley? California is projected to lose four congressional seats following the next census. Is that what you’d expect from a booming economy
Look up the June 2026 jobs numbers. California showed huge gains in employment. Texas, Arkansas, Mississippi, Idaho, Georgia all showed massive job losses.
But don’t let facts get in your way.
This misleading. While there is job growth in health and government, we are also dealing with mass layoffs, the highest unemployment in the nation and and affordability exodus that has kept our population flat. Were we booming, we would diversified employment and an increase in migration. You are fortunate to be unaffected, but many of us are truly struggling as you throw salt on our wound. —born and raised Angeleno from industry family
Growth is largely in healthcare and government in tandem with highest unemployment in the nations, mass lay-offs, and an affordability exodus that has kept our population flat. You may have yours, and that’s great, but many of don’t, so maybe don’t be so dismissive towards folks who are struggling.
this guy is the most obvious wannabe gangster. Bullying tactics don’t work on people more powerful than you.

Title: Ed Sheeran's next show, post-Macklemore, to have big police presence: report
Article_Text:
Ed Sheeran’s team is reportedly working with a beefed-up Philadelphia police detail to provide security at his Saturday show.
Sheeran’s show in the City of Brotherly Love will be the singer’s first since his supporting acts abandoned him in solidarity with opening act Macklemore. The Seattle rapper was dropped from Sheeran’s Loop Tour after expressing support for Palestinians during a recent show.
Security at Lincoln Financial Field will include “a small army of cops” inside and outside the stadium,” law enforcement sources told TMZ.
Concertgoers will reportedly pass through metal detectors and be subject to pat-downs in some cases.
Philadelphia police told TMZ, “Our officers are talking to his team to make sure all appropriate measures are taken.”
Sheeran released a statement on Monday telling fans that concert promoters pulled Macklemore off of the tour after venue owners expressed unease over the “Can’t Hold Us” vocalist’s remarks to the audience about the conflict in the Middle East.
Macklemore stirred controversy by saying “Free Palestine” during a performance at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey earlier this month. Sheeran said in his statement that he, too, has opinions on world events, but chooses not to express them on stage.
Musicians Aaron Rowe, Finneas O’Connell, Lukas Graham and Beoga reacted to that statement by showing solidarity with Macklemore and bailing from the tour’s lineup.
Sheeran is slated to perform two shows at Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts next week. The Foxborough venue is run by Robert Kraft, who is said to have been one of the owners who objected to hosting Macklemore.
Kraft said in a statement posted to X Wednesday that Sheeran asked him to pledge $2 million in relief funding to people in Gaza. After Hamas militants crossed the border to attack civilians in Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, Israeli forces invaded that Palestinian territory.
Philadelphia authorities told TMZ they’re aware of no specific threats to Sheeran.

Title: Free Library of Philadelphia Foundation president resigns
Article_Text:
President of the Free Library of Philadelphia Foundation resigns
Monique Moore Pryor was three years into the job and had clashed with staff.
Listen 1:03
From Philly and the Pa. suburbs to South Jersey and Delaware, what would you like WHYY News to cover? Let us know!
The president of the Free Library of Philadelphia Foundation is stepping down after three years on the job.
Monique Moore Pryor was hired as executive director of the foundation in 2023. She was named president in 2024.
In a joint statement issued with the foundation board, Pryor said she is resigning to “attend to pressing family matters.” Board chair Jeffry Benoliel praised Pryor for expanding and diversifying the foundation’s donor base.
“We want to thank Monique for her partnership and wish her and her family the best during this difficult time,” Benoliel said in a written statement.
The Free Library Foundation is the fundraising arm of the Free Library of Philadelphia, supporting its operations and running programs including the Author Events series and One Book One Philadelphia.
Created in 1893, the foundation never had an executive director until Pryor.
Early in her tenure, Pryor faced significant pushback from employees, particularly from the staff of the Author Events series. The staff resigned en masse in June 2024 to protest Pryor’s management and programming decisions, but the foundation board fired them later that same day.
Before Pryor was hired, the foundation began a three-year strategic planning process, which is expected to be completed next year. An interim leader will be appointed, according to the foundation, while the search for a permanent seat replacement will begin after the library completes its strategic plan.
“While any organizational change is hard, we are excited about building on the progress of the last few years and the upcoming release of the strategic plan,” Benoliel said in the statement.
Editor’s note: An earlier version of this story incorrectly reported Pryor’s title.

Title: Upper Darby restricts collaboration with ICE
Article_Text:
Upper Darby restricts collaboration with ICE in sweeping ordinance
Speakers at a meeting Wednesday night touted the importance of the ordinance in a township where nearly a quarter of residents are foreign-born.
Listen 1:08
From Delco to Chesco and Montco to Bucks, what about life in Philly’s suburbs do you want WHYY News to cover? Let us know!
Upper Darby Township Council unanimously passed legislation restricting collaboration with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement at a meeting Wednesday night.
Modeled in part on Philadelphia’s “ICE Out” legislation passed in April, the ordinance is one of the most comprehensive laws of its kind passed in the region.
Legislators and a majority of speakers during Wednesday’s public hearing touted the importance of restrictions on ICE collaboration in a municipality where nearly a quarter of the residents are foreign-born.
“It sends a clear message that our focus and priority are the people in our community,” said Upper Darby Mayor Ed Brown, who supported the ordinance. “We will follow the law, but we will do everything in our power to protect our community and keep everyone safe.”
Effective immediately, the ordinance:
- Restricts use of township resources — including police, employees, facilities, equipment, databases and other resources — for federal civil immigration enforcement, except when legally required
- Limits collection and sharing of information about someone’s immigration status
- Prevents township employees from detaining someone based on their immigration status, or because of an ICE administrative warrant or civil detainer
- Bans the township from entering into a voluntary collaboration agreement with ICE
- Prohibits township property from being used for civil immigration enforcement operations
- Requires Upper Darby police officers to identify themselves and refrain from wearing masks or face coverings, with some exceptions
- Requests federal agents identify themselves and limits assistance from township personnel if they do not do so
- Requires Upper Darby to reconsider some intermunicipal relationships with jurisdictions that sign a collaboration agreement with ICE, with some exceptions
- Requires training for all township departments on the policy
The restrictions do not apply to cases where ICE or other agents have obtained a judicial warrant for someone’s arrest, or cooperation with federal immigration enforcement agents is otherwise legally required.
A few community members at the public hearing spoke against the ordinance, questioning its impact on public safety and the threat of federal funding being withdrawn in retaliation for the policy.
Timothy Bernhardt, superintendent of Upper Darby Township Police, worked with the mayor and council members to revise and finalize the ordinance.
“Our motto is ‘the world in one place,’ and we are 68 different languages here,” he said. “Very immigrant-populated community, very diverse community. What this does, I hope, will make it clear on what we do, meaning the municipal law enforcement, and what federal authorities do.”
Upper Darby police do not enforce immigration, and have not and will not voluntarily collaborate with ICE by participating in what is known as a section 287(g) agreement, Bernhardt said.
That policy does not preclude fulfilling obligations under federal law, including detaining individuals with outstanding federal arrest warrants, Bernhardt said.
Bernhardt said he has been visiting houses of worship and other community spaces to inform immigrant residents that the police are “here to protect them,” and urging them to call 911 when needed.
“When you call 911 in this community, the Upper Darby Township Police Department is responding,” he said. “Not immigration, not Homeland Security, not anyone else. We are. And if you need our help, we will help you. We’re not there to answer your immigration status.”
Upper Darby ICE ordinance ‘important first step,’ community members say
Victoria Awotide, 24, said she was “proud of Upper Darby” for passing the ordinance. She’s lived in the township since her family immigrated from Nigeria in 2010.
She and other members of her family are U.S. citizens, but the new legislation is important for them as well as immigrant residents who lack citizenship status, she said.
“I’m glad that at least people will not be scared to just walk around their neighborhood,” she said.
Desi Burnette, a statewide coordinator with the Movement of Immigrant Leaders in Pennsylvania and a Delaware County resident, passed out signs reading “Hospitals in, ICE Out” ahead of the meeting. She said the legislation won’t end deportations in Upper Darby, but it is a “really important first step.”
“We’re a township and a community that has a lot of unmet needs,” she said. “It’s a really important statement to say that we’re not going to be using our police force, our property, or any of our resources to support ICE.”
Immigration enforcement detentions have been going on in Upper Darby well before the Trump administration, she said, and funding for ICE has steadily increased over the years under both parties. But under the current administration and with increased funding for federal immigration enforcement, ICE is “on steroids.”
“The result has been here in our community, here in Upper Darby, a lot of workers have been targeted by ICE, separated from their families,” Burnette said. “Our local businesses have been impacted negatively because people don’t want to come around.”
The environment of fear is also impacting young people, she said.
“I think we’re mostly here for our young people because we really believe that no young person or child in our community needs to feel like they don’t belong or that they’re not safe in their own community, which is something that we’ve seen happening,” Burnette said.
Editor’s note: Victoria Awotide’s name was updated to correct spelling.
